newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says not aware of any South Africa policy shift.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says not aware of any South Africa policy shift.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign ministry said on Wednesday it was not aware of any plans by South Africa, its biggest diplomatic ally, to switch recognition to Beijing.
Beijing refuses ties to states that recognise Taiwan.
South African government sources in Pretoria said on Wednesday President Nelson Mandela would announce his country's future policy on Taiwan and China later in the day.

"I don't know what to say. We have no idea about this," African affairs department chief Timothy Yang told Reuters when asked about the reports, which triggered intense speculation that a switch was in the works..
"We cannot say anything until we know what he has to say," Yang said.
South Africa is the biggest of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies, most of which are small, underdeveloped states in central America and Africa that benefit from wealthy Taiwan's generous foreign aid.

Mandela has resisted strong pressure from Beijing to drop its diplomatic ties with Taipei's exiled Republic of China government and recognise the People's Republic of China, saying he wanted good relations with "both Chinas".

Mandela's two China formulation is heresy to Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since the communists' 1949 civil war victory sent the defeated Nationalist government into exile on the island off China's southeast coast.
Beijing has obliged all nations with which it establishes diplomatic ties to drop Taiwan, though it allows diplomatic friends to maintain economic and other unofficial ties with the island.
